extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / experimental scientists (members/readers of the Royal Society, 17th-century experimentalists)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and observational standards for designing, building, and reporting experimental apparatus and experiments (optical instruments, transfusions, anatomical dissections, vegetation/sap experiments, mechanics) as illustrated in 17th-century Philosophical Transactions reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lens-grinding apparatus levelling and mounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe and construct a frame and mounting so the lens-holding pole and grinding plane are maintained horizontal and movable: e.g., a pole S passing through the centre of an inner circle B moving on pivots in an outer circle A, the frame fastened to pivots in arms fixed to the ceiling; or a pole thrust into a ball moveable within two circles; the socket must gird about the ball so it moves freely but always touches it; the centre must remain in the same situation when it moves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concentric-ring or ball-socket mounting that prevents the pole from leaving the circle (use a pin), allows raising but not unwanted lowering of the pole, and keeps the centre fixed. Mount the grinding plane (iron plate F) level on adjustable planks with regulators (square rulers in grooves), ledges for steadiness, and transverse gutters with wooden wedges to fine-adjust level; use a pendulum or leveling instrument and wedges to set true level. Note: "It is enough, if the ball do but move freely in it; yet so as always to touch it." Be aware skilled artists consider this contrivance difficult for very long glasses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polishing sequence and use of gutters
rubrics_metrics.description: After the glass has been wrought to the perfect spherical figure on the plane, continue polishing using gutters proportionable to the sphere whose semidiameter equals the length of the pole; follow rules known for grinding convex-glasses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polishing on the plane is "very long and tedious"; therefore after shaping use appropriate spherical gutters (polishers formed as gutters hollowed spherical by a wooden mould turned on a mandril) sized to the sphere. Apply paper smoothly cemented on for polishing. Follow established rules of convex-glass grinding to finish efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report animal transfusion procedures precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting transfusion experiments, give full operative procedure and matching/controls: e.g., open carotid artery of donor, let blood run into a branch of recipient jugular, pre-bleed recipient (or donor) to judged volumes, apply two ligatures near each other and cut the vein between them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include surgical steps, relative sizes of animals, how much blood was drawn, the order of bleeding and transfusion, placement of ligatures, and immediate post-op handling (untie and observe). Report survival and later anatomical findings (e.g., wound healing, vein joined by fibres, presence of communicating branch). This level of detail allows readers to evaluate procedural adequacy and possible confounders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report functional outcomes and time-course
rubrics_metrics.description: Record functional and behavioral outcomes with time course after interventions (e.g., in transfusion: mobility, appetite, return of hearing), with dates and progressive observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give concrete behavioral markers and timelines (hours/days/weeks), e.g., animal remained on table an hour, leapt down and sought masters, within two days ran about, appetite returned, by 13 June nearly cured of deafness, etc. These observations serve as primary outcome evidence; include any variability (not always consistent responses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscope performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify optical design and measurable performance: lens arrangement (two plano-convex glasses touching convex surfaces), whether image appears flat, magnifications at adjustable lengths (listed: 41×, 60×, 111×, 143×), and field diameter (given per setting: e.g., 8 inches 7 lines; 12 in. 4 lines; 13 in.; ~16 in.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing or evaluating a microscope, report construction details, whether objects are shown 'flat and not crooked', magnification factors at each adjustment, and the diameter of the visual field measured on the object-plate. Report observed resolving capacity (e.g., detecting minute animalcules in grains of sand). These metrics allow quantitative comparison between instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomical demonstration standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Settle anatomical controversies by careful examination, comparative dissections, and illustrative figures: show structures (e.g., testicle made of a 'congeries of minute vessels' vs glandular), provide labelled figures for human and animal subjects, and trace functional pathways (semen secreted in tubuli → vasa efferentia → epididymis → vas deferens → vesiculae seminales).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear dissections, comparative plates, explicit labelling (A A, B B, etc.), and reasoned argument from observation to conclusion. Use consistent anatomical terminology and map observed structures to functional claims. Report where species differ (human vs boar) and note possible counter-interpretations by contemporaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental design: isolate explanatory mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Design experiments to distinguish competing causal explanations (e.g., Boyle aims to show phenomena attributed to nature's abhorrence of vacuum may be explained by gravity or by the 'spring' of air).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the competing hypotheses and perform trials that demonstrate whether each phenomenon can arise from different mechanisms (weight of superincumbent atmosphere vs spring of included air). Aim to separate variables and avoid conflating causes. Report which aspects are shown by which mechanism and any limitations of separation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical analysis must use current methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical/analytical accounts should reflect the current state of the science to be of interest (critic: Hydrologia Chymica's account of Scarborough waters is 'not such as can be in the least degree interesting to the chemical reader of the present day' due to imperfect chemistry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure analytical methods are adequate and up-to-date; otherwise state methodological limitations. Readers will judge chemical accounts by rigor and currency of analytical techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vegetation experiment reporting and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting propagation and sap-running experiments, specify species, precise planting/propagation technique (e.g., put branches wrong end downwards, cover two or three joints, cut stem near top joint, have joint half covered), conditions for rooting, and success/failure across species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List which species succeed with which methods (elders, briars, willows, vines, currants, etc.), give procedural details (how much to bury, when to cut, care of knots/joints), and include negative results and hypotheses for failure (gumminess of apple/pear juices). This helps reproducibility and interpretation of species-specific responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sap-tapping procedural details and observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Record where sap ascends (inner bark), seasonal timing (late January to mid May; species-specific dates), best time of day (about noon), effects of incision (girdling kills tree above incision), and dependence on rain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report practical tapping details: vent size (small vents may allow night-and-day run), timing per species (poplar/asp early, walnut later), and observed phenomena (sap may run in hard frost for sycamore). Note cautions (certain incisions kill the tree) and preservation methods (gatherers' experience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnographic and natural-history reporting norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Document local practices, durations, remedies, and toxic properties observed in the field (e.g., pearl-divers can stay ~quarter hour underwater; an expert diver takes a pint of strong-water before diving; lignum aloes is venomous to the eye and skin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete local details (how long, preparatory customs), stepwise methods (drying, bruising, steeping roots, alembic distillation for oils), precise observed effects (blinding if milk drops in eye; scabby sores on skin), and geographic occurrence. Such specifics allow assessment of reliability and potential hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement and derivation of mechanical laws with assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: When presenting laws of motion, state axioms and derive proportional relations clearly (e.g., if agent A produces effect E then m·A produces m^n·E; 'if the power V move the weight P then the force mV will move mP ...'; degrees of celerity proportional to lengths; consequences for machine construction: augment weight and celerity must diminish in same ratio so product mass×celerity remains constant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide stepwise numbered propositions with algebraic relations, explain units/assumptions (same space/time), and relate abstract laws to practical machine construction (trade-off between mass and velocity). When treating collisions, specify cases (direct, oblique, elastic vs inelastic) and give formulae for resulting celerities and impetuses; note how obliquity alters impulse via geometric factors (radius to secant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collision analysis: exchange of impetus and restitution conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: In collision accounts, state how bodies exchange motion: bodies with 'proper velocities' retain them after collision; bodies with 'improper velocities' are restored to equilibrium by collision so that excess is transferred (e.g., impetus products PC, mPC; in elastic bodies restitution may cause them to recede).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit the concept of impetus (mass×velocity) and show algebraic accounting of momenta before and after, including direction signs. State applicability (hard bodies move together; elastic bodies may separate depending on restoring forces) and handle oblique impacts by resolving components and applying geometrical corrections.
